fields.explanation: The displayed automorphisms on the based free group would have to commute for a direct-product action. At the original generator b their images are ba and ab. Mathlib FreeGroup.lift extends the maps and a permutation quotient separates the two actual free-group elements. This addresses the literal action formula, not an outer action or a repaired version.
fields.flaw: The stated formulas define the induced action of the direct-product group Γ = Z/3Z × Z/2Z on π₁ ≅ F₂.
fields.problem: Title: Genus Bounds for Harmonic Group Actions on Finite Graphs
fields.source_context:
0056 | \address{Lawrence University, Department of Mathematics, 711 E. Boldt Way, Appleton, WI 54911, USA}
0057 | \email{corrys@lawrence.edu}
0058 | 
0059 | \maketitle
0060 | 
0061 | \begin{abstract}
0062 | This paper develops graph analogues of the genus bounds for the maximal size of an automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g\ge 2$. Inspired by the work of M. Baker and S. Norine on harmonic morphisms between finite graphs, we motivate and define the notion of a harmonic group action. Denoting by $M(g)$ the maximal size of such a harmonic group action on a graph of genus $g\ge 2$, we prove that $4(g-1)\le M(g)\le 6(g-1)$, and these bounds are sharp in the sense that both are attained for infinitely many values of $g$.
0063 | \end{abstract}
0064 | 
0065 | \section{Introduction}
0066 | 
0067 | In the papers \cite{BN1} and \cite{BN2}, M. Baker and S. Norine study the category of finite graphs with harmonic morphisms as a discrete analogue of the category of Riemann surfaces with holomorphic maps. The cornerstone of the analogy is the Riemann-Roch theorem of \cite{BN1}, which allows for an Abel-Jacobi theory concerning the map from a graph to its Jacobian (see also \cite{BHN} for a different approach). Baker and Norine go on to derive a Riemann-Hurwitz formula in \cite{BN2}, and use it to investigate hyperelliptic graphs and Weierstrass points.  This paper furthers the analogy by establishing graph analogues of the genus bounds for the maximal size of an automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g\ge 2$. The classical story is as follows: for each $g\ge 2$, define
0068 | $$
0069 | N(g):= \max\{|\Aut(X)| \ | \ X \textrm{ is a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$}\}.
0070 | $$
0071 | Then $8(g+1)\le N(g)\le 84(g-1)$, and these bounds are sharp in the sense that both the upper and lower bound are attained for infinitely many values of $g$. The upper bound $84(g-1)$ was found by Hurwitz in \cite{H}, and the fact that it is sharp was proven by Macbeath in \cite{M}. The lower bound and its sharpness was proven by Accola in \cite{A}, and the techniques of loc. cit. provide the model for many of the arguments in the present paper. Indeed, once armed with the Riemann-Hurwitz formula from \cite{BN2}, the main complication in the graph-theoretic situation is the presence of vertical ramification, which has no analogue in the context of Riemann surfaces.
0072 | 
0073 | By a \emph{graph} we will always mean a finite, connected multigraph without loop edges. Thus, multiple edges between two vertices are allowed, but no vertex can have an edge to itself. We denote the edge-set and vertex-set of a graph $G$ by $E(G)$ and $V(G)$ respectively. As in the case of Riemann surfaces, we define the \emph{genus} of a graph $G$ to be the rank of its first Betti homology group, $g(G)=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1$. This number is the dimension of the cycle-space of $G$, and is more commonly refered to as the cyclomatic number of $G$.
0074 | 
0075 | With this terminology, let $M(g)$ be the maximal size of a harmonic group action (see Definition \ref{Hgrpaction}) on any graph of genus $g\ge 2$. This paper is devoted to proving the following theorem:
0076 | 
0077 | \begin{theorem} \label{Main}
0078 | For $g\ge 2$ we have $4(g-1)\le M(g)\le 6(g-1)$. In fact, $4(g-1)$ and $6(g-1)$ are the only values taken by the function $M(g)$, and both values are obtained for infinitely many values of $g$.
0079 | \end{theorem}
